issues.legal_issue: A ground available in an earlier proceeding but not raised there is barred when raised in a later proceeding challenging the same acquisition.
material_facts: The petitioner had earlier brought a writ petition concerning the acquisition, in which the declaration was set aside because he had not received notice of the inquiry into objections, and the matter was sent back for that inquiry.

The petitioner later challenged the renewed declaration and relied on the contention that it had been published outside the applicable time limit, although that contention had been available in the earlier proceeding and was not raised there.
issues.conclusion: The later time-limit contention was barred by constructive res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies constructively to bar a matter that was available to be raised in an earlier proceeding but was not raised.

predicates.successive_writ_challenge: A person brings a later writ proceeding challenging the same acquisition action that was involved in an earlier proceeding.
predicates.ground_available_in_earlier_proceeding: The legal ground relied on in the later proceeding was available to the person during the earlier proceeding.
predicates.ground_omitted_from_earlier_proceeding: The person did not raise that legal ground in the earlier proceeding.

issues.definition: When a person brings a later writ challenge to the same acquisition action and omits a ground that was available in the earlier proceeding, that ground is barred.

issues.legal_issue: A court-ordered stay of dispossession during a pending challenge to an acquisition notification is excluded when calculating the time allowed for publishing the acquisition declaration, even without an express order staying publication.
material_facts: A land-acquisition notification was published on May 17, 1984, and an initial declaration was later set aside after the petitioner was found not to have received notice of the inquiry into objections.
After the inquiry and consideration of objections, a renewed declaration was published on June 15, 1989.

During the petitioner’s later challenge to the validity of the acquisition notification, the High Court stayed dispossession; that stay remained in force while the challenge and ensuing appeals were pending.
The stay order did not expressly prohibit publication of the declaration, but the court held that the period during which the stay operated had to be excluded from the applicable three-year period.
issues.conclusion: The period during which the stay of dispossession operated was excluded from the publication period, and the renewed declaration was valid when calculated on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The first proviso to Section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984, imposed the applicable time limit for publication of a declaration; Explanation I required exclusion of the period during which action or proceedings pursuant to the acquisition notification were stayed by a court. A stay of dispossession during a pending challenge to the notification’s validity qualifies for that exclusion even if it does not expressly stay publication of the declaration. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_acquisition_declaration_case: The proceeding concerns a declaration made in a land-acquisition process.
predicates.declaration_subject_to_publication_deadl: The declaration is subject to a time limit for publication.
predicates.court_stayed_dispossession_during_notifi: While a person’s challenge to the acquisition notification was pending, a court ordered that possession not be taken.
predicates.declaration_published_within_deadline_af: After the period covered by the court’s stay is excluded, the declaration was published within the applicable time limit.

issues.definition: A declaration subject to a publication deadline is valid when a court stayed dispossession during a pending challenge to the acquisition notification and the declaration was published within the deadline after excluding the stay period.
